title: What Is Your Homeschool Style?
description: Answer 10 quick questions to discover your dominant homeschool style.

CL.title: Classical
CL.summary: You thrive with structure, deep learning, and clear academic progression.
strengths: You value mastery and consistency.
You are intentional about academic rigor.
You create dependable rhythms for your family.

CM.title: Charlotte Mason
CM.summary: You lean toward rich books, short focused lessons, and heart-level learning.
strengths: You nurture wonder and attention.
You prioritize meaningful conversations.
You blend academics with beauty and nature.

UN.title: Unit Study
UN.summary: You love connecting subjects around shared themes and real-life projects.
strengths: You make learning feel connected and practical.
You are strong at project-based teaching.
You naturally adapt to family-wide learning.

TR.title: Traditional
TR.summary: You prefer proven classroom-like methods and measurable progress.
strengths: You value clarity and accountability.
You keep expectations consistent.
You prefer structured pacing.

ON.title: Online
ON.summary: You value digital tools and flexible platform-based learning.
strengths: You are resourceful with ed-tech tools.
You scale learning with online systems.
You support independent digital progress.

US.title: Unschooling
US.summary: You trust natural curiosity and prioritize intrinsic motivation.
strengths: You build ownership and confidence.
You reduce pressure and preserve joy.
You are responsive to each child's unique pace.

HY.title: Hybrid
HY.summary: You blend methods based on season, child, and subject.
strengths: You are highly adaptable.
You personalize learning with wisdom.
You balance structure and flexibility well.

questions.question: When planning your homeschool week, what feels most natural?

options.text: A clear schedule with specific subjects each day
Short meaningful lessons with books and narration
A theme everyone can explore in different ways
Following the child's interests as they unfold
Mixing structure and flexibility based on the day

questions.question: What is your ideal role during learning time?

options.text: Instructor with a clear lesson plan
Guide who sparks reflection and discussion
Facilitator of projects and hands-on discovery
Mentor who supports child-led exploration
Coach who adjusts approach as needed

questions.question: How do you usually choose curriculum?

options.text: Comprehensive, proven programs with progression
Living books and rich ideas over worksheets
Resources that can connect across subjects
Minimal curriculum, mostly real-life learning
Different tools for different children/subjects

questions.question: When your child resists a lesson, what is your first instinct?

options.text: Keep the expectation but adjust pacing
Pause and reconnect through conversation
Shift to a creative or practical activity
Let interest lead and revisit later
Try a different method entirely

questions.question: What does a successful homeschool day look like to you?

options.text: Core subjects completed with solid understanding
Deep ideas discussed and habits nurtured
Meaningful project progress with family collaboration
Child highly engaged in self-directed learning
We adapted and still moved forward

questions.question: How do you feel about testing and assessments?

options.text: Useful for tracking mastery and gaps
Prefer narration, observation, and discussion
Prefer project outputs over traditional tests
Mostly unnecessary for daily learning
Use whichever method fits the context

questions.question: Which environment helps your child learn best?

options.text: Consistent routine with predictable blocks
Calm rhythm with books, nature, and reflection
Interactive spaces for experiments and projects
Real-world settings and everyday experiences
A mix depending on mood and goals

questions.question: When introducing a new topic, you usually start with:

options.text: Definitions, sequence, and core concepts
A compelling story or great book
A hands-on challenge or mini project
Questions your child already has
Whatever approach fits that topic best

questions.question: What is your biggest homeschool priority this season?

options.text: Academic depth and skill progression
Character formation and love of learning
Integrated learning that feels meaningful
Autonomy, confidence, and curiosity
Sustainable rhythms that actually work

questions.question: How do you make curriculum decisions when life gets busy?

options.text: Preserve core sequence and trim extras
Focus on essential books and habits
Consolidate into one strong unit or project

Pivot quickly and mix what serves us
